ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertex A of the right triangle \(Rt\triangle ABO\) is the intersection point in the second quadrant of the hyperbola \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) and the line \(y=-x-(k+1)\). \(AB \perp x\)-axis at B, and the area of the triangle \(S_{\triangle ABO}=\frac{3}{2}\). Determine the coordinates of the two intersection points A and C of the line and the hyperbola.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Combine the analytic expressions of the two functions into a system of equations, $\begin{cases}y=-\frac{3}{x}\\ y=-x+2\end{cases}$. Solving this, we find: $\begin{cases}x_1=-1\\ y_1=3\end{cases}$ and $\begin{cases}x_2=3\\ y_2=-1\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore$ the coordinates of point A are $\boxed{\left(-1, 3\right)}$, and the coordinates of point C are $\boxed{\left(3, -1\right)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, and A is located in the second quadrant; from A a perpendicular is drawn to the x-axis, intersecting at B, so AB is a vertical line segment, OB is on the x-axis, and △ABO is a right triangle. In the figure, a hyperbola has two branches in the second quadrant and the fourth quadrant, and a straight line with negative slope intersects the hyperbola at A in the second quadrant and at C in the fourth quadrant. Reasoning: Let A=(x_A,y_A). From the structure in the figure, OB=|x_A|, AB=|y_A|, so S_{△ABO}=1/2|x_Ay_A|=3/2, obtaining |x_Ay_A|=3. Also A is on the hyperbola y=k/x, therefore x_Ay_A=k. A is in the second quadrant, x_A<0, y_A>0, so k=x_Ay_A<0, hence k=-3. Substituting into the equations of the hyperbola and the straight line, obtain y=-3/x, and y=-x-(k+1)=-x-(-2)=-x+2. Combining -3/x=-x+2, multiplying both sides by x gives -3=-x^2+2x, that is x^2-2x-3=0, which factors as (x-3)(x+1)=0, so x=-1 or x=3. From y=-x+2 obtain the corresponding y=3 or y=-1. According to the figure, A is in the second quadrant, A=(-1,3); the other intersection point C is in the fourth quadrant, C=(3,-1).
